pll2d3c3-d1e3514.summary: States that angels shared equally being spirits, indissoluble and immortal, while differing in subtlety of essence, understanding, and freedom of will; only God, who made all in measure, number, and weight, can grasp these distinctions.

pl-l2d3c3.summary: Notes what angels shared equally: being spirits, indissoluble, and immortal; they differed in subtlety, wisdom, and freedom. Only God, who made all in measure, number, and weight (Wis 11:21), can grasp these invisible distinctions.
claims: All angels are equally spirits, indissoluble, and immortal.
Angels differ in subtlety, wisdom, and freedom.
Only God can comprehend these differences.
